tasks.title: Start every call at once
tasks.description:
Implement `runToolCalls(registry, calls)` in `src/parallel.ts`.

For each call, get the content with `executeToolCall(registry, call.function.name, call.function.arguments)` and build `{ role: 'tool', tool_call_id: call.id, content }`. Return all the messages.

The calls must run at the same time: start every one before waiting for any. The check uses slow tools that record how many calls are running at once, and expects all of them to be in flight together.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.ts` and note how long the stock check takes.
Turn each call into a promise of its tool message.
Wait for all of the promises together.
hints: An `await` inside a `for` loop waits for each call before the next one starts. That is the slow version.
`calls.map(async (call) => ...)` gives you an array of promises that have all started already.
`Promise.all` on that array waits for every one and resolves with an array of tool messages.

tasks.title: Answer in a fixed order, matched by id
tasks.description:
Calls finish whenever they finish. A quick scan beats a slow one. Your result must not depend on that.

`runToolCalls` returns the messages in the order of the `calls` array, and each message carries the id and the result of its own call, whatever order they finished in. A call that fails (for example, an unknown tool) still gets its error result in its own place, and the others still get theirs. An empty list gives an empty array.

The check makes calls finish in reverse order, repeats the same tool with different arguments, and puts an unknown tool in the middle.
nextSteps: Think about what decides the order of your output array.
Make sure each message is built from its own call, not from a shared variable.
Run the demo and compare the ids with the order of the calls.
hints: Pushing each message into an array when its call finishes records the finishing order, not the call order.
`Promise.all` keeps the order of the promises you give it, no matter which settles first.
`executeToolCall` never throws, so one failing call cannot reject the whole `Promise.all`. Keep it that way.

tasks.title: Put the parallel runner in the loop
tasks.description:
`runAgent` in `src/agent.ts` still runs the calls of each reply one after another. Change it to answer each reply with `runToolCalls`.

Each round, the next request must hold the assistant message with all its tool calls, followed by exactly one tool message per call, in call order. Keep the `registry` option, the step limit and the `{ answer, steps }` result.

The check asks Pip for stock checks that it requests all in one reply, and runs a scripted model with three slow tools to see that they run at the same time.
nextSteps: Find the inner `for` loop that runs the calls.
Replace it with one call to `runToolCalls`.
Append the tool messages it returns, then run the demo again.
hints: Only the part between pushing the assistant message and the next request changes.
`runToolCalls` wants function tool calls. Filter `reply.tool_calls` on `type === 'function'` first.
Spread the result into the conversation: `messages.push(...(await runToolCalls(registry, calls)))`.
